parts.title: The name, and where it begins
parts.intro: A surname written down under eight sovereigns, in four languages, and spelled at least nine ways, and the place where every account the family gives of itself begins: the valleys of Carnia, where the documents run out. This part reads the name, then the mountain villages, then Istria town by town, then the historian of the province, whose letter answers, in his own hand, most of what the archive has spent its time trying to establish.

parts.title: Seven families, one surname
parts.intro: The archive follows seven families of the name. They arrive from different directions and the records join no two of them. This part separates a family, which is an origin, from a station on one family's road and from a namesake, then takes the others in turn: the castle parish of Svetvinčenat, the Dalmatian line out of Venice, the Cretan estate at Seget, southern Istria, Vodnjan, the Kvarner households, Dubrovnik, Corsica and the Alpine clusters of Trentino.

parts.title: Leaving, and the ground they left
parts.intro: Three movements across five centuries: weavers walking south out of the mountains, two men arriving at one port in the same eighteen months, and a twentieth-century scatter across four continents. Passenger manifests and naturalisation petitions follow the name abroad; imperial, naval and shipping paper show the work it did; the burial registers and the graves show where it lies; and seven walks go to the ground itself.
